name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 127 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 35% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata.
status.nb: 127 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 35 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Kolkata.

summary.en: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan is reviewing the security situation in Jammu and Kashmir, calling for a decisive blow against terror and anti-infiltration measures while meeting top security officials. In Manipur, security forces rescued a man abducted for 20 days, arrested a PLA cadre and seized two phones, and destroyed 160 acres of illegal poppy plantations. In Chhattisgarh, forces recovered Rs 39.77 lakh from an underground Maoist cache. A member of the LG security team was killed in an accident in Ambala. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Unionens innenriksminister Govind Mohan vurderer sikkerhetssituasjonen i Jammu og Kashmir, og etterlyser et avgjørende slag mot terror og anti-inntrengings-tiltak mens han møter topp sikkerhetsoffiserer. I Manipur reddet sikkerhetsstyrkene en mann som var bortført i 20 dager, arresterte en PLA-medlem og beslagla to telefoner, og ødela 160 mål ulovlige opiumsplantasjer. I Chhattisgarh gjenvant styrkene 39.77 lakh rupee fra en underjordisk maoist-cache. Et medlem av LG-sikkerhetsteamet ble drept i en ulykke i Ambala. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
